systems.name: Relay v1 brain
systems.summary: Wanders, hunts, searches, chases, breaks doors; never leaves the map.

systems.name: Director (alarm panel)
systems.summary: Scoring core in main, not wired; predates the 10-07 to 10-14 rules (phone walk, unlock 6 m, sight tests, no rehang).

systems.name: Away, arrive, withdraw
systems.summary: It leaves, stays away, and returns at least 42 m from you.
systems.closed_note: Decided: v2 approved, after the Alpha (10-21)

systems.name: Noise meter
systems.summary: Sprints, barges and slams add up and call it; walking is almost free.

systems.name: Quiet-player sweep
systems.summary: After 240 s with no call it patrols the zone ahead of you.

systems.name: Tiers
systems.summary: v1: by zones visited plus a stall. v2: one tier per 150 new cells.

systems.name: Test bots
systems.summary: A tool: seeded bots measure the Relay before and after each step; its 15 measurement fixes are in main since 10-08. The 10-22 smoke on v1 passed 8 of 8 (C05); the full matrix waits on a new yes.

systems.name: Path hearing
systems.summary: Sound follows real paths: a shut door or window adds 9 m; walls block.

systems.name: Sense links
systems.summary: A heard noise gives a rough estimate, never your exact spot.

systems.name: Eyes and spotting
systems.summary: A 120° head cone to 12 m; a meter that fills faster up close.

systems.name: Lock-on and chase
systems.summary: Warnings first, a 0.7 s hold and chime; chase capped at 4.4 m/s.

systems.name: Sight tests, prompt gate
systems.summary: Prompts hide only for threats the player can perceive.

systems.name: Warning stages
systems.summary: Walking distance to the Relay sets stages 0 to 2; drives the W1 lamps since 10-22.

systems.name: Stage 1: your lamps
systems.summary: Your room's lamps dip together, never near it (on v1 since 10-22); Stutter and Failing lamps sit out the bursts (hotfix 10-22). The ballast groan comes with 声音设计.

systems.name: Stage 2: muffled steps
systems.summary: Its steps through walls, muffled by doors; a hum when it stands still. Built and measured in 声音设计's clone (steps +10.3 dB over room tone through a shut door); lands with the C10 pass after the Alpha cut.

systems.name: Stage 3: lock-on
systems.summary: A door-holder thunk and one chime when it sees you.

systems.name: Extra cues
systems.summary: Device sounds, a panel tick, the hum returning, an edge marker.
systems.closed_note: Decided: all; marker off by default (10-21)

systems.name: Chase wave
systems.summary: Lamps ripple out from your room when a chase starts.

systems.name: Wallpaper arrows
systems.summary: The print's arrows turn toward the station TV, then the EXIT (C24 = A + A20), and run with a chase. The motion pick is open again (C31).
systems.closed_note: Decided: yes (10-07); the exit is set (10-21)

systems.name: Screens join warnings
systems.summary: Parked, not in v1 (C09, Red 10-22): CRTs would show interference at stage 1 and an alarm slate in a chase. Screens never sag or roll with the lamps.

systems.name: Warnings on today's Relay
systems.summary: W1 lamps live on today's Relay (10-22). The W2 pass (steps, stingers and clicks out, tension by stage, the drone gated, the WarnBurst groan) is packaged and lands after the Alpha cut.

systems.name: Doors: E open, shut
systems.summary: Doors open on E and shut; each is a noise heard to about 20 m. Decided 10-22: double-acting, always swinging away from the opener (after the Alpha).
systems.closed_note: Decided: swing away from the player (10-22)

systems.name: Ease, barge, slam, ajar
systems.summary: Walk to open softly; sprint to barge or slam; the Relay leaves doors ajar.

systems.name: Broken doors
systems.summary: Broken for the run; E on it is refused, silent (0.55 s guard, since 10-21). B·4 crosshair, the shut-try look and sound, and the strings BROKEN / WON'T SHUT (C11) to build.

systems.name: Glass and climbing
systems.summary: Hold E to break a pane through staged cracks (a loud call, since 10-21); walk into the frame to climb.

systems.name: Quiet sash pry
systems.summary: Hold E on the latch for 4 s: a quiet way through a window.

systems.name: Alarmed windows
systems.summary: Foil-taped windows that always call the Relay.

systems.name: Door, lock, key models
systems.summary: 57 models in main, not placed by the map; door rig, key assembly and 3 materials still missing.

systems.name: Locked doors
systems.summary: Locks, rattle, key-turn shot; today it locks every door or none.

systems.name: Keys
systems.summary: Look and press E on desktop (walk over on phones). Today one per zone, opening nothing; decided 10-22: one floor key per floor, at the station.

systems.name: Map, zones, modules
systems.summary: Generated zones, rooms as data, streaming, the Level Designer.

systems.name: Trigger rooms
systems.summary: Rooms you can read from the doorway; entering sounds an alarm.

systems.name: Sanctuaries
systems.summary: Dead-circuit rooms the Relay will not enter.

systems.name: Relay entries
systems.summary: Where it arrives and leaves; markers live, dead-end entries to build.

systems.name: Map validator
systems.summary: Checks keys can be reached, windows stay passable, cover exists.

systems.name: Office dressing
systems.summary: Cubicles, CRTs, piles and wall outlets (in the maze since 10-22); terminal host desks to come.

systems.name: Evacuation plan
systems.summary: One printed sheet by the start door; EXAMINE reads it. Red picked sheet A on 10-22: a route diagram that teaches four rules and the locked stair (a Phase 0 variant until the lock lands). Art handed off; Game visuals packs it.

systems.name: EXAMINE close-up
systems.summary: E frames the plan or the first key; the game pauses (in main since 10-22); the sound mix and a focus-loss guard remain.

systems.name: Office terminals
systems.summary: One readable computer per Office zone; E to read its pages.

systems.name: Crosshair states
systems.summary: One grammar for door, lock, broken door and the look-eye; the map's AimKind feed is in main (10-21). Strings and the E·1 eye decided 10-22.

systems.name: Key and lock HUD motion
systems.summary: The key slides in; the lock opens at the crosshair.

systems.name: Desk monitors
systems.summary: The ad plays on desk monitors today (since 10-14); decided 10-22: still screens in the maze, the ad only on the title and station TVs.

systems.name: Exit and win
systems.summary: One locked EXIT per floor; the floor key opens it; a stairwell behind it leads one floor deeper; a run ends only when caught.
systems.closed_note: Decided: an EXIT per floor leads deeper (10-21)

systems.name: Exit signs
systems.summary: Lit, dim and loose EXIT signs; a LIT-locked one goes over each floor's EXIT, chevron signs in its zone later.
systems.closed_note: Decided: a lit sign over the exit door, chevrons in its zone later (10-22)

systems.name: Way-out route
systems.summary: The route the arrows point: the station until the floor key is taken, then the EXIT; one field shared with the TV beacon, glass impassable, never reads the Relay. Spec v1.0 in main (10-22); code after the Alpha.
systems.closed_note: Decided: the station first, then the EXIT (10-22)

systems.name: Plan legend
systems.summary: The plan's legend; sheet A (picked 10-22) marks the stair as EXIT and holds the wall-arrow glow back until W6 ships.

systems.name: Plan and alarm pages
systems.summary: A floor plan and alarm history on terminals, later.

systems.name: Touch controls
systems.summary: USE button, tap to open, three gaits; walking is heard on phones.

systems.name: Reduce flashing, captions
systems.summary: Lamp changes ramp slower; sounds get captions.

systems.name: More settings
systems.summary: Lamps still, warning-cue volume, visual sound cues, screen effects.

systems.name: Photosafety limits
systems.summary: No lamp may flash more than 3 times a second. Not yet true for ambient lamps: a Tall-hall Stutter lamp chatters at 9 flashes/s (small area); the limiter lands after the Alpha.

systems.name: WebGL tier
systems.summary: A separate, lighter web build; never changes desktop.

systems.name: Station and TV beacon
systems.summary: One station per floor: the only TV playing, heard through the building. Its rack holds the floor key; taking it kills the TV and calls the hunter.

systems.name: Tutorial floor
systems.summary: Floor 1 teaches the loop: the station just past the EXIT, no locked inner doors, the hunter held until the key is taken, a lamp burst before any chase.

decisions.question: Do screens join the warning language?
decisions.recommendation: No in v1
decisions.rationale: Asked by 平面视觉 · 广告 as its SCREENS §4 question. Why not in v1: each cue keeps one meaning, the lamps and steps are not even in yet, and a third channel would muddy what the next playtest can tell apart. The tutorial TV beacon (N6, 10-22) is a broadcast, not a warning: it ducks under every warning, so "one meaning per cue" still holds.
decisions.answer: 1: not in v1. TVs stay ambience and the tutorial beacon a broadcast; the lamps (W1) and steps (W2) carry the warning, one meaning per cue. SCREENS §4 is parked; the 10-14 rule stays: screens never sag or roll on FixtureChanged or LampDipped

decisions.question: Wire lamp and step warnings to today's Relay as a bridge?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, before the next playtest; drop the any-range 2D state stingers at the same time.
decisions.rationale: W1 and W2 must be built for v2 anyway, and they read WarnStage, which today's hunter already computes (in main since 10-08), so almost nothing is thrown away. It lets the playtest check item 07 ("noticed it before it reached me") and the LIGHT cue. The baseline shows stage 0 still holds 64-81 % of on-map time at tier 1, so the lamps will not dip all the time. Limit: today's chases start on first sight, with no G3 gate, so a warning is honest but not yet guaranteed. The 2D Hunt/Search/Chase stingers and the straight-line heartbeat say "near" at any range, so they go when W1 and W2 land (sound clean-up items 1, 2 and 4), not later with UsesArrive. Testers asked for radar or position sound (10-11); the rule stays: no radar. W2's steps are real 3D sound from where it is. W1 is about half a day for 关卡设计 alone (SetLampOverride and WarnStage are in main). W2 waits on 声音设计: a new event, or a gain on the Relay's existing through-wall steps. The 2D stingers go in the same sound pass as W2.
decisions.answer: Yes, before the next playtest: W1 lamps first, W2 steps when 声音设计 delivers; the 2D stingers go with W2

decisions.question: Broken-door strings: BROKEN / WON'T SHUT?
decisions.recommendation: Yes: BROKEN, and WON'T SHUT on a shut try; 平面视觉 sets the type
decisions.rationale: Asked by 平面视觉 (UI/UX) inside its one prompt-strings question (E · UNLOCK / KEY 14, BROKEN / WON'T SHUT, the EXAMINE verbs). Until then the map gives a broken door no prompt (since 10-21).
decisions.answer: Yes: BROKEN when aimed; WON'T SHUT as line 2 during the 0.55 s reaction to a shut try, while the door icon swings; the phone verb is BROKEN

decisions.question: Keys on boards: walk over, or look and press E?
decisions.recommendation: Look and press E (E · TAKE KEY) for every key; fix the 33° aim bug first.
decisions.rationale: Keys hang on a wall board, so walking over them reads oddly. HUD key B lifts from the held key and the first key opens EXAMINE: both already assume E. Cost: the code exists (KeyPickupNeedsE, off); phones keep walk-over until the touch tap path can target keys (today it ignores triggers; 交互设计 adds map.KeyOnRay and AimKind.TakeKey), so desktop flips first. Walk-over costs nothing now but breaks those two flows.
decisions.answer: Look and press E for every key; desktop first, phones once the tap path can target keys; fix the 33° aim bug

decisions.question: Which doors lock?
decisions.recommendation: About 1 in 3, after the key check
decisions.rationale: Fixed per seed. Locks switch on only once the validator (L5) proves every key can be reached; until then keys stay off (doorsNeedKeys 0). Key rule, 关卡设计's default: the key of the zone you stand in opens all its doors and is never used up. On v1 the open after a key turn keeps the normal door noise and trying a locked door stays silent; unlock and rattle become 6 m with v2's verb noise table (ease 6, barge 18, slam 27).
decisions.answer: About 1 in 3 per seed, on only after L5; the zone key opens all its doors; v1 noise unchanged, 6 m with v2 (key rule replaced by A13 on 10-22: one floor key per floor; Floor 1 has no locked inner doors)

decisions.question: What is the exit, and can a run end in escape?
decisions.recommendation: An EXIT on each floor leads one floor deeper; a run still ends only when caught.
decisions.rationale: Keeps Red's 10-02 rule (a run does not end; it gets harder) and gives the goal 8 of 9 testers could not name. EGRESS fits: a fire stair leads to the next floor of the same building. It gives the arrows (C08), the EXIT signs (C23) and the route (C24) a target. Rough cost: 关卡设计 2 to 3 days for the map and game minimum (a map-built stairwell room: the exit door shuts and locks behind you like the start door, the old map is released, a new seed starts at the stairwell's far door, the tier carries over, a FLOOR count on CAUGHT, a placement rule reachable without glass). Not included: the EXIT sign in the map and the stairwell look (游戏视觉), the arrows (C08, +1 to 2 days), strings and type. An escape that ends the run costs about the same plus an ending, and breaks the 10-02 rule. No exit costs nothing, but the goal problem stays and C08, C23, C24, N4 and N5 point at nothing.
decisions.answer: Each floor has an EXIT; through it a stairwell leads one floor deeper; a run still ends only when caught (since 10-22 the EXIT is locked and the floor key opens it: A13)

decisions.question: Where do EXIT signs go: Office door signs, ceiling?
decisions.recommendation: A lit EXIT sign over each floor's EXIT door now; chevron hanging signs inside the exit's zone later
decisions.rationale: 游戏视觉's pick. The exit door's sign is locked to LIT (never half-lit, loose or dead), with the crossbar on the leaf: about 1 h visual, 0.5 day map. Chevron signs hang over each opening one step closer to the exit, inside its own zone only (Hanging at ceilings of 2.65 m or more, HangingFlush at 2.27 m or more), static per seed, never on windows: about 1 day visual and 1 to 1.5 days map, after the stairwell minimum. Short range, so not a radar; NFPA 101-1988 asks for them where the exit is not visible. No Office door signs: those carry room numbers.
decisions.answer: 游戏视觉's two steps: a LIT-locked EXIT sign over each floor's EXIT door now; chevron hanging signs inside the exit's zone after the stairwell

decisions.question: Confirm the way-out route rule once the exit is set
decisions.recommendation: Point the route at the floor's EXIT; while its chunk is unbuilt, the nearest border doorway toward it
decisions.rationale: 关卡设计's rule. Distances come from a path field seeded at the EXIT door, with hearing's costs but glass impassable, so the cue never points at a window (§9.6). It never reads the Relay, so it is not a radar. Forged FLOW from tier 4 (EGRESS, 10-03) is in question since 10-22: a forged arrow would pull away from the station and the EXIT, against A20, so 叙事设计 asked Red to retire it (C29). The EXIT sits 14 to 22 cells of walking from the floor's start door, so the fallback mostly serves players who wander off.
decisions.answer: A: the route points at the floor's EXIT; while its chunk is unbuilt, the nearest border doorway toward it (amended by A20 on 10-22: the station first, then the EXIT)

One FloorLabel(floor) function makes either a one-place change; until Red answers, the strings use B. Asked by 叙事设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-22: record the answer only from Red's words there.

decisions.rationale: Red turned it ON on 10-03 (research/wallpaper_motion/20_level_design_phosphor.md §15 Q4; mark M10 in 30_narrative_phosphor.md): from tier 4 a forged FLOW chevron, glowing under a lit lamp, leads into a dead end. Since 10-22 the arrows lead to the station and then the EXIT (C24, A20), and RELAY §9.6 keeps tiers from making the hints worse. Asked by 叙事设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-22: record the answer only from Red's words there.

decisions.ref: C10 scope; RELAY §13 sound items 3 and 5
decisions.question: Also fix the two other through-wall "near" sounds now, in 声音设计's W2 pass, not in v2?
decisions.recommendation: 1, both now: tension follows the warning stage; the drone plays only at stage 2 or in sight, muffled like the steps
decisions.rationale: C10 (Red 10-21) moved §13 items 1, 2 and 4 to now: the 2D stingers, the release clicks and the straight-line heartbeat, because they say "near" through any number of walls. Items 3 and 5 have the same flaw but stayed with v2 (gated on UsesArrive): (5) tension = state weight x straight-line proximity, so the HumBed beating swells as the Relay closes in through walls; (3) the presence drone [LOW DRONE] is always on while released, louder with straight-line proximity. Their v2 forms are approved (C02, C06): tension 0.05 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 1.0 by stage, rise 1/s, fall 0.25/s; the drone gated to stage >= 2 or PlayerSeesRelay with the steps' path gain and muffle, the proper coil hum still in v2. No new hooks (WarnStage is in v1). Options: 1 both now; 2 tension now, drone in v2; 3 both in v2. 声音设计 builds them as separable parts, so no answer causes rework. Asked by 系统设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-22.
decisions.answer: 1: both now, in 声音设计's W2 pass: tension follows the warning stage (0.05 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 1.0), and the presence drone plays only at stage 2 or in sight, muffled like the steps, until v2's coil hum (apply_c10.sh --c30 both)

decisions.question: Which prompt strings ship with the stair key?
decisions.answer: As drafted: key panel STAIR KEY / OPENS THE STAIR DOOR; locked stair door LOCKED / NEEDS STAIR KEY, with the key E · UNLOCK / STAIR KEY (phone UNLOCK); close-ups E · READ PLAN / READ SCREEN / READ SIGN, E · EXAMINE KEY, E · TAKE KEY. No RUN, HIDE or relay on screen

decisions.question: Keep E·1, or switch to E·3 because the open eye may read as 'being seen'?
decisions.answer: Keep E·1. A playtest question asks what the eye meant; if testers read it as being seen, switch to E·3 (parameters only)

glossary.definition: The director’s noise meter for one run. Player noises add to it: sprint step +3, barge +8, slam +12, pry +8, ease a door or unlock +1, walking 0. It drains 3 per second (2 at tier 5), starting 3 s after the last noise. At the threshold (60 at tier 1, down to 45 at tier 5) the Relay is called to the area of the noise, never to the exact spot.

How much threat the player has perceived in the current encounter. Only perceived cues count: lamps +1/s, steps +2.5/s, seeing the Relay +4/s, the chase +6/s, a lock-on +15. At the peak the director holds for 4 s (SUSTAIN), then fades the encounter and the Relay withdraws.
A difficulty step. Today it rises with zones visited plus a stall rule; v2 proposes one tier per 150 newly explored cells. Tiers make the Relay better, never the warnings shorter.

The Relay may lock on only after the warning has run continuously for at least 3 s (stage 1 or higher), including at least 1 s of continuous stage 2 (steps). The timers reset when the stage drops. Only a lock-on at touching distance (1.5 m) is exempt.

The Relay’s distance to the player along real walking paths (a shut door adds 9 m), never more than three times the straight line. It sets the warning stages: stage 1 at 30 m or less, stage 2 at 18 m or less.
The guaranteed calm after the Relay leaves: 100 s at tier 1, 60 s at tier 5. Noise cannot call it back during RELAX; glass and alarm devices still can.

The Relay may break a door only if a sound it heard came through that door, or it saw the player cross it or heard it move. It may quietly open the doors that were shut on its route when it was sent. Any other shut door is a wall to it.
When a quiet player goes 240 s (tier 1) without a call, the director sends the Relay to patrol a zone ahead of them, aimed at the area, never the exact spot.
The warning level in the player’s own room: 0 nothing, 1 lamps dip, 2 muffled steps, 3 the lock-on chime.
The director sending the Relay toward an area, because Attention crossed its threshold, a device was tripped, or a sweep is due.
